source_caption:
When Children of Heaven was released in 1997, no one expected a quiet little film from Iran to make Oscar history. Yet it became the first Iranian movie ever nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. It did not rely on spectacle or big cinematic moments. It reached audiences around the world through something much simpler and more powerful: pure emotion.

Directed by Majid Majidi, the story centers on a problem that sounds almost too small to carry an entire film. A young boy named Ali loses his sister Zahra’s only pair of shoes after picking them up from the cobbler in a busy Tehran neighborhood. That single mistake quietly sets everything in motion.

Ali and Zahra come from a modest working class family. Their father struggles to find steady work and constantly worries about rent and debt, while their mother is ill and overwhelmed at home. Money is so tight that even basic groceries feel like a burden. When the shoes go missing, the children keep it a secret because they know their parents simply cannot afford another pair.

They come up with a plan to share Ali’s sneakers. Zahra wears them to school in the morning, then rushes home so Ali can wear them for his afternoon classes. These simple runs through crowded streets become surprisingly tense, turning an ordinary school day into something urgent.

As the story unfolds, it becomes more than just about shoes. When Ali discovers that third prize in a local race is a new pair of sneakers, he trains with one goal in mind: winning them for Zahra. There are no villains or dramatic twists, just everyday life seen through children forced to grow up too quickly. The film’s power lies in its honesty, its quiet love between siblings, and its reminder that even the smallest struggles can carry the deepest emotions.

source_details.synopsis: Children of Heaven (Persian: بچه‌های آسمان, romanized: Baččehā-ye āsmān) is a 1997 Iranian family drama film written and directed by Majid Majidi. The plot follows a brother and sister, and their adventures over a lost pair of shoes. It received positive reviews, and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film in 1998.
